scope: NCollection_UBTree::TreeNode::Kill member assignment, link publication and detached subtree payload destruction over the current checked arena facade
source_scope: UBTree/EBTree/filler source, shared destruction guards, selected tests and native probes; not full compiler or allocator dependency closure.

method_bindings.domain: Live checked node identifiers with children and index 0 or 1. In-place bounds then object clone_from; original parent retained; surviving child links committed after assignment, grandchildren reparented before destruction.
Detached killed branch only. Preorder payload destruction, child zero before child one; native paired allocation and deferred paired frees remain outside this binding.

behavior: Kill no longer copy constructs a survivor and replaces the whole parent. Bounds.clone_from runs before object.clone_from at original destination field addresses, with no spurious parent destruction or Clone callback.
If either assignment callback fails, native and Rust retain the old live child links; partially changed bounds/object values match the native exception traces.
After successful assignment, Kill publishes the retained child links and reparents surviving grandchildren before destroying the old survivor. Parent identity remains unchanged.
Old survivor payloads are destroyed first, then killed subtree payloads in preorder: current node, child zero, child one. Each object is destroyed before its bounds at its original allocated address.

Detached AllocatedBox owners transfer to the existing NativeNodeOwner deallocation guard. Even when a Rust payload destructor panics, allocation and incremental live lease are released; DeferredDestructorPanic drains the detached branch before resuming the first panic.

The destructor-panic drain is a Rust ownership safety extension, not native throwing-destructor parity. The native fixture throws only during assignment before any ownership graph mutation or destruction.

Native destructor callbacks directly confirm grandchildren already point at the retained parent. Rust has no safe reentrant public tree metadata observer; final link tests and the explicit reparent-before-release source sequence establish the implemented phase order, not an equivalent observer API.

compatibility.evidence: ubtree.rs and ubtree_filler.rs are byte-identical to branch base. Existing borrowed payload drop-check, covariance, public field partial move and positive auto-trait compile tests run unchanged in both normal and Miri sweeps. No new bound or public signature changes.
compatibility.checked_extensions: Dead node ids, leaves and out-of-range child indices return without callbacks. Native only defines the live leaf/no-op and valid branch index domain.

remaining_gaps: Gemmate still uses separate arena allocations and cloning rather than native paired allocation/default construction/member assignment. Native Kill releases paired arrays after payload traversal; current Rust frees each individually allocated node as it is destroyed. No allocation bytes, allocation count or pair-free timing parity is credited.
Clear and UBTree automatic destruction still use arena insertion order, not native delNode traversal/deferred pair frees. This receipt does not change or close those paths.
TreeNode destructor-body child-pointer clearing and raw Child/Parent pointer projections remain open; checked identifiers and Rust borrowing do not provide native reentrant pointer observer access.

Moved-from allocator null state, native dangling last pointer behavior, filler equal-slot assignment effects and borrowed filler insertion/canonical tree construction remain as prior receipts describe.

Arbitrary C++ generic payload ABI and address-sensitive construction are not claimed. Rust clone_from models assignment only for payload implementations that supply the corresponding assignment semantics.
No global API or legacy declaration credit is added; full TreeNode, UBTree and UBTreeFiller parity remains incomplete.
validation_history: Initial draft attempted a direct unsafe release_typed_node call and was rejected by the crate unsafe-code lint before tests ran. Final implementation reuses existing NativeNodeOwner with no new unsafe code. Initial native fixture used a nonexistent ChangeRoot shorthand; corrected to const_cast of Root on a nonconst tree. Final native matrices, normal tests, docs, strict Clippy/fmt and strict Miri cover final sources. Miri emitted existing downstream ElementCast unstable-name-collision warnings but no errors.
